summary.intent: Fix a false-positive CI failure where the stale `release-as` pin guard was incorrectly flagging the release-please PR (#528) as having stale version pins.
summary.outcome: Confirmed that the guard false-positives on the release PR because release-please bumps manifest versions to match `release-as` (making them equal, which the guard treats as stale). Fixed by gating the live check off `release-please--*` branch PRs in ci.yml while keeping the unit tests unconditional.

repo: The stale-pin guard (`check-stale-release-as.js`) compares `release-as` in `release-please-config.json` against the current manifest version; equal values signal a forgotten/stale pin on normal PRs but are expected on the release-please PR itself.
The release-please PR always uses branch name `release-please--branches--main` with author `cipherbox-release-bot` and `separate-pull-requests: false` (single PR).
The stale-pin guard is invoked exclusively in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lint job (lines 71-74) and only triggers on `pull_request` to main — never on push.
On main, `release-as` values are always strictly ahead of manifest versions (pending targets); on the release PR they become equal after release-please bumps the manifest.
Phases 52 (FUSE durability/at-rest safety) and 54 (E2E test infra typing — migrating .mjs helpers to .ts) were merged in this pull.

code.finding: Lint job stale-pin steps split into two: unit test step (always runs) and live check step gated with `if: "!startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-please--')"`

workflow: When a guard compares config-vs-manifest state, it can't distinguish 'about to ship' from 'already shipped and forgotten' without context about the branch — the branch name is the right discriminator.
Gating the live check (not the unit tests) off the release branch preserves coverage: stale pins on feature PRs still surface, but the release PR is not false-flagged.
actionlint pre-existing warnings (lines 459, 485) were noted but intentionally left out of scope to keep the change minimal.

friction: The guard had no mechanism to distinguish a legitimate in-flight release (release-as == manifest is expected) from a genuinely stale forgotten pin — both produce the same equality condition.
open_items: Two pre-existing actionlint warnings in ci.yml (lines 459, 485) were identified but not addressed — left as known tech debt.
